FIX / BUILDOUT: these are live reads on every run, without a cache or download exception handler. Record input versions / dates, validate schema and preserve reproducible dated snapshots.
note: slices copy existing station rows only. They do not add missing dates. A full 1999-2005 calendar has 2,557 days; actual source row counts may differ.
note: 2001-2003 has 1,095 calendar days. Each station has its own record length / raw column set. Clean comparison tables have 5 columns and a DATE index.
note: coverage counts usable observations, not snowfall amount. 60 months x 11 columns: 5 metrics per station plus expected days. Leap years are handled by days_in_month.
note: 12 months x 11 columns. Counts use actual month lengths. A high donor count alone does not establish agreement or station interchangeability.

note: the missing-run cell can be executed independently after the earlier comparison tables exist. It uses MSP / Falls only and does not reference the misnamed donor variable.
note: each result is R x 3: start, end, days. R varies by station / variable. Reindexed absent dates and quality-rejected observations both count as missing.
BUILDOUT: no assignments replace target observations; no to_csv or savefig executes. Do not treat the gap investigation as an implemented splice.

BUILDOUT: decide and implement replacements explicitly
Inspect overlapping target / donor observations, exact dates, variable-specific quality and potential station differences. Distinguish SNOW (new snowfall) from SNWD (snow depth).
Choose missing-only replacement or another documented rule. Keep target values where the rule requires; do not blindly copy all donor columns or add snow depth as snowfall.
Preserve original target data and log target / donor IDs, dates, variables, old and new values, flags and reason. Save derived spliced observations and diagnostics. Connect that output to the analysis input explicitly.

VERIFY / downstream handoff
Historical diagnostics suggested MSP gaps around 2000-2004 and Falls gaps in 2002. Recheck exact spans and donor availability against the selected snapshot; saved outputs alone do not verify current source execution.
Compare results with and without accepted splices. Preserve full historical acquisition / storage; trim phase-one results to 1950 onward in downstream analysis.
The four-season, La Nina / neutral, SD, missing-data reporting and Kenny-table requirements remain downstream tasks. Splicing must preserve the daily values, dates, units and quality information those tasks need.
